new_entities.name: American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius)
new_entities.description: Standardized American ginseng extract used acutely or chronically for cognitive enhancement.

new_entities.name: Acute working memory performance
new_entities.description: Working-memory task performance measured within hours of a single intervention dose.

edges.population: healthy young and middle-aged adults receiving standardized Panax quinquefolius extracts
edges.mechanism: American ginseng may support acute working memory through cholinergic modulation, ginsenoside-driven frontoparietal activation, and possibly later microbiome-mediated effects with repeated intake. Across human trials, the signal is most consistent for working-memory tasks rather than broad global cognition.
edges.summary: American ginseng has one of the cleaner acute cognitive signals among botanicals in this brief: small randomized crossover trials repeatedly report working-memory benefits within hours of dosing. The evidence is still based on modest sample sizes and a fairly narrow extract literature, but the consistency is better than for many other nootropics.
edges.caveats: Most of the literature comes from a small cluster of related Cereboost trials, so independent replication is still thinner than ideal. Effects are task-specific and do not imply a broad enhancement of every cognitive domain.

evidence.notes: Effects of American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius) on neurocognitive function: an acute, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study.

evidence.citation: Reay JL et al 2015 Hum Psychopharmacol
evidence.notes: Improved working memory performance following administration of a single dose of American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius L.) to healthy middle-age adults.

evidence.citation: Lee J et al 2022 Eur J Nutr
evidence.notes: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial investigating the acute and chronic benefits of American Ginseng (Cereboost®) on mood and cognition in healthy young adults, including in vitro investigation of gut microbiota changes as a possible mechanism of action.
